summary: The plan is ready to execute. This pass covers the plan only; it approves no code or runtime result. All three accepted round-1 suggestions are now in the plan. R1-01: PLAN.md:207-213 sets the order preflight/pilot, then screening, then confirmation (including any extra blocks the decision needs), then optional diagnostics. Incomplete confirmation gives no recommendation, and the envelope counts the diagnostics. R1-02: PLAN.md:177-184 uses extra time blocks only for within-cell variability above 10%. If each placement is repeatable but their rankings disagree, the result is reported as placement sensitivity. R1-03: PLAN.md:141-148 allows at most two re-creation attempts. If the layout still repeats, confirmation is incomplete. Overlap fractions are recorded and OST selection stays automatic. I checked the revision and found nothing new that breaks the design. The plan's stripe layouts still match evidence.txt. My own recount of the arithmetic matches the plan: 54 screening + 54 confirmation primary trials, and 69 full-dataset-equivalent diagnostic scans (about 21.1 TiB). Deferring R1-04 is acceptable within the bounded scope. Buffered single-worker reads can still spread across stripes through client readahead, so the 1-worker single-file diagnostic is still informative. The response also correctly promises no isolated multi-worker single-file conclusion, and the primary 40-worker case already exercises 8 workers per file. Not adopting the prior reviewer's rough OST-total and node-DRAM remarks is justified, because no decision rule depends on them. I found no blocking scientific or feasibility flaw. Two optional wording/clarity notes follow.

Primary arithmetic: confirmation 3 counts x 2 placements x 3 worker counts x 3 blocks = 54; 108 x 313 GiB ≈ 33 TiB; 0.94-4.7 h at 10-2 GiB/s; storage 6 x 313 = 1878 GiB ≈ 1.83-1.84 TiB (rounding) and 9 x 313 = 2817 GiB ≈ 2.75 TiB

Bounded-scope feasibility: the worst-case total (primary + diagnostics ≈ 7.7 h of timed I/O at 2 GiB/s, plus staging, hashing and eviction) can exceed the 12 node-hour cap, but the stated priority order and the 'incomplete means no recommendation' rule handle this safely

findings.evidence: The plan says to 'recreate that campaign copy up to two times within the resource cap' but does not say whether the repeated copy is deleted before re-creation or kept until a different layout is obtained. Deleting it first may let the allocator pick the same OSTs again. Keeping it temporarily holds a tenth copy set (~3.06 TiB, above the stated 2.75 TiB envelope).
findings.requested_change: Optionally say which order is used. If the old copy is kept during re-creation, note the transient storage of up to one extra copy set (~313 GiB) in the headroom check.

findings.evidence: The text calls the one-worker single-file run 'a diagnostic for single-file benefit'. Because R1-04 was deferred, the only supported claim is single-worker, buffered single-file behaviour (responses-01.md:16-17).
findings.requested_change: Optionally reword it as a 'single-file, single-worker diagnostic' so the deliverable cannot be read as an answer about multi-worker per-file stripe parallelism.
